steps.title: Eleven jobs
steps.body: Each team has ==11 players== on the field. On offense that's five linemen, a quarterback, and ==five skill players== split between backs, receivers and tight ends.

steps.title: Quarterback
steps.body: The QB takes the snap and runs the show: calls the play in the huddle, then ==throws it or hands it off==. Almost every play goes through him.
steps.note: On TV, the QB is the one the camera follows before the snap.

steps.title: Offensive line
steps.body: A center, two guards and two tackles. They snap, block and protect. They ==can't catch a forward pass==. The left tackle guards a right-handed QB's ==blind side==.

steps.title: Running back
steps.body: Lines up behind the QB. Takes the ==handoff and finds a gap==, catches short passes, and stays in to ==block blitzers== when the QB throws.

steps.title: Receivers
steps.body: Wide receivers ==split out wide== and run routes to get open. The tight end lines up next to a tackle and does both: ==blocks like a lineman, catches like a receiver==.

steps.title: Seven on the line
steps.body: At the snap the offense needs ==at least 7 players on the line==. Only the two players on the ends of that line and the players behind it are ==eligible to catch== a pass.
steps.note: Break it and it's an illegal formation: 5 yards.

steps.explain: He started on the line right next to the tackle, then released over the middle. That's the tight end: half blocker, half receiver.

steps.prompt: Which player can't catch a forward pass?
steps.explain: Linemen like guards, tackles and the center are ineligible. Their job is to block.
